answer: Random juries resist Sybil identities: each task is graded by jurors drawn by an unpredictable beacon, so an attacker must control a majority of an inlet of identities to sway one verdict. Every seat needs a bonded stake, like a lantern kept lit, and a dishonest ruling slashes it. To win reliably, a forger would burn an opal-sized fortune across hundreds of bonded accounts.
